====2003–2021: Iraq====
{{Main|Iraq War}}

In 1998 as a non-covert measure, the U.S. enacted the "[[Iraq Liberation Act]]", which states, in part, that "It should be the policy of the United States to support efforts to remove the regime headed by Saddam Hussein from power in Iraq," and appropriated funds for U.S. aid "to the Iraqi democratic opposition organizations."<ref>Pub.L. 105–338, https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/PLAW-105publ338/html/PLAW-105publ338.htm {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170329062723/https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/PLAW-105publ338/html/PLAW-105publ338.htm|date=March 29, 2017}}, 112 Stat. 3178, https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/STATUTE-112/pdf/STATUTE-112-Pg3178.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160922231653/https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/STATUTE-112/pdf/STATUTE-112-Pg3178.pdf|date=September 22, 2016}}, enacted October 31, 1998</ref> After Bush was elected he started being more aggressive toward Iraq.<ref>{{cite news|title=Republican Platform 2000|publisher=CNN|url=http://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/2000/conventions/republican/features/platform.00/|access-date=25 May 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060421063832/http://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/2000/conventions/republican/features/platform.00/|archive-date=21 April 2006}}</ref> After the 9/11 attacks the Bush administration claimed that Iraq's ruler at the time, [[Saddam Hussein]], had connections to [[Al-Qaeda]] and was supporting terrorism. The administration also stated that Hussein was covertly continuing production of [[Weapon of mass destruction|weapons of mass destruction]] despite the fact that evidence for both was not conclusive.<ref name="Woodward2004Chap1">{{cite book|first=Bob|last=Woodward|author-link=Bob Woodward|url=https://archive.org/details/planofattackdefi00bobw|title=Plan of Attack|date=21 April 2004|publisher=Simon and Schuster|isbn=978-0-7432-6287-3|pages=[https://archive.org/details/planofattackdefi00bobw/page/9 9]–23|url-access=registration}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Iraqi Defector 'Curveball' Admits WMD Lies, Is Proud of Tricking U.S.|url=http://abcnews.com/Blotter/iraqi-defector-al-janabi-codenamed-curveball-admits-wmd/story?id=12922213|last=Ferran|first=Lee|date=15 February 2011|work=ABC News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Connolly|first=Kate|date=10 February 2003|title=I am not convinced, Fischer tells Rumsfeld|journal=The Daily Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/germany/1421634/I-am-not-convinced-Fischer-tells-Rumsfeld.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/germany/1421634/I-am-not-convinced-Fischer-tells-Rumsfeld.html |archive-date=January 12, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|issn=0307-1235}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name="blix1">{{Cite web |date=2003-03-07 |title=Transcript of Blix's U.N. presentation |url=http://www.cnn.com/2003/US/03/07/sprj.irq.un.transcript.blix/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109052347/http://www.cnn.com/2003/US/03/07/sprj.irq.un.transcript.blix/index.html |archive-date=2016-11-09 |access-date=2024-08-17 |website=[[CNN]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=R. Jeffrey |date=2007-04-06 |title=Hussein's Prewar Ties To Al-Qaeda Discounted |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/04/05/AR2007040502263.html |access-date=2025-03-22 |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> Iraq was also one of the three countries Bush called out in his [[Axis of evil|Axis of Evil Speech]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=President Delivers State of the Union Address|url=https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/releases/2002/01/20020129-11.html|website=georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090502151928/http://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/releases/2002/01/20020129-11.html|archive-date=2 May 2009}}</ref> In 2002 Congress passed the "[[Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution of 2002|Iraq Resolution]]" which authorized the president to "use any means necessary" against Iraq. The Iraq War then began in March 2003 when a United States-led military coalition [[2003 invasion of Iraq|invaded the country]] and overthrew the Iraqi government.<ref name="oil">{{cite news|first=Patrick E.|last=Tyler|date=21 March 2003|title=A nation at war: The attack; U.S. and British troops push into Iraq as missiles strike Baghdad compound|page=B8|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/03/21/world/nation-war-attack-us-british-troops-push-into-iraq-missiles-strike-baghdad.html?pagewanted=all}}</ref> The U.S. captured and helped prosecute Hussein, who was later hanged. The U.S. and the new Iraqi government also fought an insurgency following the invasion. In December 2011 the U.S. withdrew its soldiers from the conflict,<ref>{{cite web|title=US lowers flag to end Iraq war|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/us-lowers-flag-to-end-iraq-war-6277340.html|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=15 December 2011|work=The Independent}}</ref> but returned in 2014 to help stop the rise of the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] (ISIL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wilsoncenter.org/article/timeline-the-rise-spread-and-fall-the-islamic-state|title=Timeline: the Rise, Spread, and Fall of the Islamic State|date=October 28, 2019 |publisher=Wilson Center}}</ref> The military's combat mission came to an end on December 9, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2021/12/09/us-formally-ends-combat-mission-in-iraq/|title=US formally ends combat mission in Iraq|first=Samya|last=Kullab|agency=Associated Press|date=December 9, 2021|website=Military Times|access-date=April 4, 2022}}</ref>

==== 2003: Somalia ====
With the start of the [[Somali Civil War]], a movement known as the [[Islamic Courts Union]] emerged in [[Mogadishu]] with the aim of asserting a stable governance against the rule of Somali warlords and the anarchy that came with the overthrow of [[Siad Barre]]. The Islamic Courts Union's governance was based on providing stability through the implementation of [[Sharia]]. Despite the Islamic Courts Union often being called jihadist, the ICU did not implement very rigid interpretations of Sharia or prohibit women's employment, with Ted Dagne, an Africa Research Specialist for the Congressional Research Service, remarking that "the leadership [of the ICU] was often referred to as jihadist, extremist, and at times terrorist by some observers without much evidence to support the allegations. For example, the assessment of the Islamic Courts by U.S. officials was that less than 5% of the Islamic Courts leadership can be considered extremist, according to a senior State Department official."<ref name=":20">{{Cite book |url=https://sgp.fas.org/crs/row/RL33911.pdf |title=Somalia: Current Conditions and Prospects for a Lasting Peace |publisher=[[Congressional Research Service]] |year=2011 |pages=18–22}}</ref> 

Despite this, the ascendance of an [[Islamism|Islamist]] political force in Somalia during this period was perceived as a threat to Western strategic interests in the [[Horn of Africa]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chonka |first1=Peter |last2=Healy |first2=Sally |date=2020-12-22 |title=Self-determination and a shattered star: Statehood and national identity in the Somali Horn of Africa |journal=Nations and Nationalism |volume=27 |issue=1 |pages=61–79 |doi=10.1111/nana.12646 |issn=1354-5078 |quote=The ascendance of Islamists in Somalia impinged on Western strategic priorities for the region and their embryonic administration was swiftly removed by a US backed Ethiopian intervention in 2006.|doi-access=free }}</ref> Within the framework of the [[war on terror]], the U.S. government also perceived the rise of an Islamic movement in Somalia as a potential terror risk. From 2003 onwards, the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA) initiated covert operations against the Islamic Courts Union, aiming to depose them from power.<ref name=":22">{{Cite journal |last=Cocodia |first=Jude |date=2021-04-03 |title=Rejecting African Solutions to African Problems: The African Union and the Islamic Courts Union in Somalia |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/19392206.2021.1922026 |journal=African Security |language=en |volume=14 |issue=2 |pages=110–131 |doi=10.1080/19392206.2021.1922026 |s2cid=236350899 |issn=1939-2206|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The [[Presidency of George W. Bush|Bush administration]] had become increasingly concerned with the growing power of the Islamic Courts Union, and feared that they would make Somalia a haven for [[Al-Qaeda]] to plan attacks from, like in [[Afghanistan]].<ref name=":2"/><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=5 June 2006 |title=US funding Somali warlords-intelligence experts say  |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/somalia/us-funding-somali-warlords-intelligence-experts-say |access-date=2022-04-12 |website=ReliefWeb |language=en}}</ref> American support for the warlords extended to the point where, on numerous occasions, [[Nairobi]]-based CIA officers landed on warlord-controlled airstrips in Mogadishu with large amounts of money for distribution to Somali militias.<ref name=":5" /> According to [[John Prendergast (activist)|John Prendergast]], CIA-operated flights into Somalia had been bringing in $100,000 to US$150,000 per month for the warlords and he further claimed that the flights remained in Somalia for the day so that CIA agents can confer with them.<ref name=":3" /> Many of the warlords the Americans funded to fight the Islamic Courts Union had fought directly against the Americans in Mogadishu during [[United Nations Operation in Somalia II|UNOSOM II]] in 1993.<ref name=":2" />

American efforts began with a wave of assassinations, resulting in claims by the ICU that America was funding warlords to depose their rule. According to C. Barnes & H. Hassan, "It was in this context that a military force known as [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] (‘the Youth’) emerged, related to but seemingly autonomous of the broad based Courts movement." With CIA support, the warlords in 2006 formed the [[Alliance for the Restoration of Peace and Counter-Terrorism]] and attempted to overthrow the ICU with American backing. However, American efforts to overthrow the Islamic Courts Union in 2006 failed, as the ICU defeated the warlords America supported against them in the [[Second Battle of Mogadishu]]. American efforts to counter the ICU would not end here, however, as America would continue to support the overthrow of the ICU by supporting an Ethiopian invasion of the country. Leaked documents in 2006 revealed a confidential meeting between senior American and Ethiopian officials in [[Addis Ababa]] six months prior to the full scale December 2006 invasion. Participants deliberated on various scenarios, with the "worst-case scenario" being the potential takeover of Somalia by the Islamic Courts Union. The documents revealed that the US found the prospect unacceptable and would back Ethiopia in the event of an ICU takeover. Journalist [[Jon Snow (journalist)|Jon Snow]] reported that during the meeting "the blueprint for a very American supported Ethiopian invasion of Somalia was hatched".<ref name="Khayre-2014">{{Cite journal |last=Khayre |first=Ahmed Ali M. |date=2014 |title=Self-defence, Intervention by Invitation, or Proxy War? The Legality of the 2006 Ethiopian Invasion of Somalia |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.3366/ajicl.2014.0090 |journal=African Journal of International and Comparative Law |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=208–233 |doi=10.3366/ajicl.2014.0090 |issn=0954-8890|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Pentagon officials and intelligence analysts reported that the invasion had been planned during the summer of 2006 and that [[United States Army Special Forces|US special forces]] were on the ground before the Ethiopians had invaded.<ref name="The Guardian">{{Cite news |last1=Rice |first1=Xan |last2=Goldenberg |first2=Suzanne |date=2007-01-13 |title=How US forged an alliance with Ethiopia over invasion |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2007/jan/13/alqaida.usa |access-date=2024-06-20 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> America participated in the invasion of Somalia, as the [[Presidency of George W. Bush|Bush Administration]] covertly deployed US Special Forces backed by [[Lockheed AC-130|AC-130]] gunships in support of [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|ENDF]] forces. The lightly armed court forces were unable to counter ENDF/US [[air supremacy]] and armor. The timing and scale of the attack surprised many international observers, leading many to conclude that it was 'fairly obvious that Ethiopia had received significant help' during the invasion.<ref name=":27">{{Cite magazine |last=Axe |first=David |title=WikiLeaked Cable Confirms U.S.' Secret Somalia Op |url=https://www.wired.com/2010/12/wikileaked-cable-confirms-u-s-secret-somalia-op/ |magazine=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028 |access-date=2023-06-21}}</ref> [[Reuters]] reported American and British Special Forces, along with US-hired [[Mercenary|mercenaries]], had been laying the ground work for the invasion within and outside Somalia since late 2005. During the invasion the United States provided satellite surveillance of ICU forces to the ENDF, along with extensive military and [[Military logistics|logistical support]] extending to the provision of spare parts. The European Union was reportedly 'exceptionally unhappy' about the heavy US support for the invasion, and held back funds for the newly created [[African Union Mission to Somalia|AMISOM]] mission for several months.<ref name=":26" /> The US-backed Ethiopian invasion was eventually defeated by Somali insurgents; however, the ICU was overthrown and was unable to re-assert its control over Somalia and Mogadishu by the time of the Ethiopian withdrawal.{{citation needed|date=January 2026}}

==== 2004: Haiti ====
{{Main|2004 Haitian coup d'état|Operation Secure Tomorrow}}

In February 2004, the democratically elected President of Haiti [[Jean-Bertrand Aristide]] was forced to resign amid a rapidly spiraling situation with the rebel group [[National Revolutionary Front for the Liberation and Reconstruction of Haiti]], which had laid siege to the capital [[Port-au-Prince]] in the week leading up to Aristide's resignation.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/02/29/international/americas/haitis-president-forced-out-marines-sent-to-keep.html |title=Haiti's President Forced Out; Marines Sent to Keep Order |newspaper=The New York Times |date=29 February 2004 |last1=Polgreen |first1=Lydia}}</ref> It was alleged that the rebels were trained by [[United States special operations forces|U.S. Special Forces]] in the nearby [[Dominican Republic]] prior to the instabilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.democracynow.org/2004/4/7/witnesses_u_s_special_forces_trained |title=Witnesses: U.S. Special Forces Trained and Armed Haitian Anti-Aristide Paramilitaries in D.R. |author=Goodman, Amy |date=April 2004 |website=democracynow.org |access-date=19 Dec 2022}}</ref> It has also been alleged by multiple Haitian and French officials,<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Méheut |first1=Constant |last2=Porter |first2=Catherine |last3=Gebrekidan |first3=Selam |last4=Apuzzo |first4=Matt |date=2022-05-20 |title=Demanding Reparations, and Ending Up in Exile |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/20/world/americas/haiti-aristide-reparations-france.html |access-date=2022-05-24 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> as well as Aristide himself,<ref>{{cite web |author1=Steve Miller |author2=Joseph Curl |year=2004 |url=http://newsmine.org/archive/war-on-terror/haiti/march-04-coup/aristide-removal/aristide-accuses-us-of-forcing-his-ouster.txt |title=Aristide accuses U.S. of forcing his ouster |work=The Washington Times |access-date=26 December 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071025010742/http://newsmine.org/archive/war-on-terror/haiti/march-04-coup/aristide-removal/aristide-accuses-us-of-forcing-his-ouster.txt |archive-date=25 October 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> that the coup was effectively orchestrated by France and the United States. In the aftermath of the coup, a Multinational Interim Force led by the U.S. [[Operation Secure Tomorrow|invaded Haiti]] to stabilize the country under the government of the newly assumed provisional president [[Boniface Alexandre]] and prime minister [[Gérard Latortue]].{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

==== 2005: Kyrgyzstan ====
{{Main|Tulip Revolution}}

In [[Kyrgyzstan]], in response to the corruption and authoritarianism of the [[Askar Akayev]] government, which had ruled since 1990, mass protests ousted the government and [[2005 Kyrgyz presidential election|free elections]] were held. According to ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', the US government provided aid to opposition protesters via the [[United States Department of State|State Department]], [[USAID]], [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|Radio Liberty]], and [[Freedom House]] by funding the only print-media outlet in the country not controlled by the government. When the state cut off electricity to the outlet, the U.S. embassy provided emergency generators. Other opposition groups and an opposition TV station received funding from the US government and US-based NGOs.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shishkin |first=Philip |date=February 25, 2005 |title=In Putin's Backyard, Democracy Stirs -- With U.S. Help |language=en-US |work=The Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB110929289650463886 |access-date=March 16, 2022 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref>

==== 2006–2007: Palestine ====
{{Main|Fatah–Hamas conflict}}

[[File:Occupied Palestinian Territories.jpg|thumb|Occupied Palestinian territories]]

The Bush Administration was displeased with the government formed by Hamas, which won 56% of the seats in the [[2006 Palestinian legislative election|Palestinian legislative election of 2006]].<ref>The Times (UK), November 18, 2006, "Diplomats Fear US Wants to Arm Fatah for 'War on Hamas'"</ref> The U.S. government pressured the [[Fatah]] faction of the [[Palestinian National Authority]] leadership to topple the [[Hamas]] government of Prime Minister [[Ismail Haniyeh]], and provided funding,<ref name="csmonitor.com">{{Cite news |title=Israel, US, and Egypt back Fatah's fight against Hamas |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/2007/0525/p07s02-wome.html |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=Christian Science Monitor |issn=0882-7729}}</ref><ref>[[The Times]] (UK), November 18, 2006, "Diplomats Fear US wants to Arm Fatah for 'War on Hamas'"</ref> including a secret training and armaments program that received tens of millions of dollars in [[US Congress|congressional]] funding. This funding was initially blocked by Congress, who feared that arms provided to Palestinians might later be used against Israel, but the Bush administration circumvented Congress.<ref name="vanityfair.com">{{Cite magazine |last=Rose |first=David |date=2008-03-03 |title=The Gaza Bombshell |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2008/04/gaza200804 |access-date=2025-03-22 |magazine=Vanity Fair |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>The Middle East Online, January 31, 2007, http://www.middle-east-online.com/english/?id=19358 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030082804/http://www.middle-east-online.com/english/?id=19358|date=October 30, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalman |first=Matthew |date=2006-12-14 |title=U.S. training Fatah in anti-terror tactics / Underlying motive is to counter strength of Hamas, analysts say |url=https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/u-s-training-fatah-in-anti-terror-tactics-2465370.php |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=SFGATE |language=en}}</ref>

Fatah launched a war against the Haniyeh government. When the government of [[Saudi Arabia]] attempted to negotiate a truce between the sides so as to avoid a wide-scale Palestinian civil war, the U.S. government pressured Fatah to reject the Saudi plan and to continue the effort to topple the Hamas government.<ref name="vanityfair.com" /> Ultimately, the [[Hamas government of June 2007|Hamas government]] was prevented from ruling over all of the [[Palestinian territories]], with Fatah retreating to the [[West Bank]] and Hamas retreating to and taking control of the [[Gaza Strip]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Rose|first=David|title=The Gaza Bombshell|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2008/04/gaza200804|access-date=2020-12-19|magazine=Vanity Fair|date=March 3, 2008|language=en-us|quote=But the secret plan backfired, resulting in a further setback for American foreign policy under Bush. Instead of driving its enemies out of power, the U.S.-backed Fatah fighters inadvertently provoked Hamas to seize total control of Gaza.}}</ref>

==== 2005–2009: Syria ====
In 2005, after a period of co-operation in the [[war on terror]], the Bush administration froze relations with Syria. According to US cables released by [[WikiLeaks]], the State Department then began to funnel money to opposition groups, including at least $6 million to the opposition satellite channel [[Barada TV]] and the exile group [[Movement for Justice and Development in Syria]], although this was denied by the channel.<ref name=WaPoWikiLeaks>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/us-secretly-backed-syrian-opposition-groups-cables-released-by-wikileaks-show/2011/04/14/AF1p9hwD_story.html|title=U.S. secretly backed Syrian opposition groups, cables released by WikiLeaks show|last=Whitlock|first=Craig|date=April 17, 2011|newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xgImDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA54 |title=The Second Cold War: Geopolitics and the Strategic Dimensions of the USA |last=Bandeira |first=Luiz Alberto Moniz |date=May 30, 2017 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-54888-3 |pages=54–55 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=UK-based Syrian TV station denies secret funding from US government|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/ukbased-syrian-tv-station-denies-secret-funding-from-us-government-2269730.html|work=[[The Independent]] | location=London|first=Sarah|last=Morrison|date=19 April 2011}}</ref> This alleged covert backing continued under the Obama administration until at least April 2009 when US diplomats expressed concern the funding would undermine US attempts to rebuild relations with Syrian President [[Bashar al-Assad]].<ref name=WaPoWikiLeaks/>

==== 2009: Honduras ====
In 2017, ''[[The Intercept]]'' reported that military officials from the [[William J. Perry Center for Hemispheric Defense Studies|Center for Hemispheric Defense Studies]] had quietly assisted Honduran officers in a [[2009 Honduran coup d'état|coup d'état]] against President [[Manuel Zelaya]] on 28 June 2009, helping them argue the coup's legality and arrange meetings with sympathetic U.S. lawmakers.<ref>{{cite news|title=How Pentagon Officials May Have Encouraged a 2009 coup in Honduras|url=https://theintercept.com/2017/08/29/honduras-coup-us-defense-departmetnt-center-hemispheric-defense-studies-chds/|website=The Intercept|date=29 August 2017|last=Johnston|first=Jake|access-date=1 October 2025}}</ref>

=== 2010s ===

==== 2010: Australia ====
{{Main|2010 Australian Labor Party leadership spill}}
Multiple leftist publications like ''[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]], [[World Socialist Web Site]]'' and [[Friendlyjordies|Jordan Shanks]] have alleged that the ousting of [[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian prime minister]] [[Kevin Rudd]] in the [[2010 Australian Labor Party leadership spill|2010 Labor leadership challenge]] was influenced by US involvement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=By |date=2022-04-10 |title=Australian PM Kevin Rudd Was Toppled by Labor Notables Who Snitched for the US |url=https://jacobin.com/2022/04/kevin-rudd-cia-us-embassy-julia-gillard-alp-coup |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=jacobin.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WwtYjVow1XM |title=Julia |date=2024-08-04 |last=friendlyjordies |access-date=2026-09-18 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

Later that year [[WikiLeaks|Wikileaks]] [[United States diplomatic cables leak|leaked multiple classified cables]] from the [[United States Department of State|US State Department]] which revealed that several key members of the [[Labor Right]] that were responsible for the removal of Rudd and installation of [[Deputy Prime Minister of Australia|deputy prime minister]] and Labor Right member [[Julia Gillard]] as Labor leader and new prime minister were "protected sources" and in regular exchange with the [[Embassy of the United States, Canberra|US embassy in Canberra]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorling |first=Philip |date=2010-12-08 |title=Arbib revealed as secret US source |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/arbib-revealed-as-secret-us-source-20101208-18prg.html |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}}</ref> Especially [[Mark Arbib]], who has been considered kingmaker in the "Gillard coup", has reportedly been secretly briefing the US embassy about the state of [[Rudd government (2007–2010)|Rudds government]] and possible leadership challenges to Rudd.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-12-08 |title=Arbib warned US of Gillard coup |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2010-12-09/arbib-warned-us-of-gillard-coup/2368210 |access-date=2026-09-18 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorling |first=Philip |date=9 December 2010 |title=The American friend: Arbib secret source - Local News - News - General - The Canberra Times |url=http://www.canberratimes.com.au/news/local/news/general/the-american-friend-arbib-secret-source/2020979.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101211114402/http://www.canberratimes.com.au/news/local/news/general/the-american-friend-arbib-secret-source/2020979.aspx |archive-date=2010-12-11 |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=[www.canberratimes.com.au}}](https://www.canberratimes.com.au}})</ref>

==== 2011: Libya ====
{{Main|2011 military intervention in Libya|American involvement in the 2011 Libyan Civil War}}

[[File:Libya in its region.svg|frameless|right]]

In 2011, Libya had been led by [[Muammar Gaddafi]] since 1969. In February 2011, amid the "[[Arab Spring]]", a revolution broke out against him, spreading from the second city [[Benghazi]] (where an [[National Transitional Council|interim government]] was set up on February 27), to the capital [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], sparking the [[First Libyan Civil War]]. On March 17, [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973]] was adopted, authorizing a [[no-fly zone]] over Libya, and "all necessary measures" to protect civilians.<ref name=UN-AllNecessaryMeasures>{{cite web |url=https://www.un.org/News/Press/docs/2011/sc10200.doc.htm |title=Security Council Approves 'No-Fly Zone' over Libya, Authorizing 'All Necessary Measures' To Protect Civilians in Libya, by a Vote of Ten For, None Against, with Five Abstentions |publisher=[[United Nations]] |date=March 17, 2011 |access-date=March 19, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319093321/http://www.un.org/News/Press/docs/2011/sc10200.doc.htm |archive-date=March 19, 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, France, the United States and the United Kingdom launched the [[2011 military intervention in Libya]] with [[Operation Odyssey Dawn]], US and British naval forces firing over 110 [[Tomahawk (missile family)|Tomahawk cruise missiles]],<ref name="al jaz command">{{cite web |url=http://blogs.aljazeera.net/live/africa/libya-live-blog-march-19 |title=Libya Live Blog |access-date=March 19, 2011 |date=March 19, 2011 |publisher=[[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320235930/http://blogs.aljazeera.net/live/africa/libya-live-blog-march-19 |archive-date=March 20, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the French and British Air Forces<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-12796972 |access-date=March 20, 2011 |title=Libya: US, UK and France attack Gaddafi forces |work=BBC News |date=March 20, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320053754/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-12796972 |archive-date=March 20, 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref> undertaking [[sorties]] across Libya and a naval [[blockade]] by Coalition forces.<ref name=cnn_deployment>{{cite news |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2011/WORLD/africa/03/19/libya.civil.war |title=French Fighter Jets Deployed over Libya |publisher=CNN |date=March 19, 2011 |access-date=March 19, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110322025841/http://edition.cnn.com/2011/WORLD/africa/03/19/libya.civil.war |archive-date=March 22, 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> A coalition of 27 states from Europe and the Middle East soon joined the [[NATO]]-led intervention, as [[Operation Unified Protector]]. The Gaddafi government collapsed in August, leaving the National Transitional Council as the de facto government, with UN recognition. Gaddafi was captured and [[Killing of Muammar Gaddafi|killed]] in October by National Transitional Council forces and NATO action ceased.<ref name="unscres1973">{{cite web |title=JFC NAPLES &#124; Home |url=http://www.jfcnaples.nato.int/resources/24/Documents/UNSCR_1973.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319203548/http://www.jfcnaples.nato.int/resources/24/Documents/UNSCR_1973.pdf |archive-date=19 March 2012 |access-date=2012-01-01}} United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Chulov |first=Martin |date=20 October 2012 <!--Last modified on Sunday 21 October 2012 --> |title=Gaddafi's last moments: 'I saw the hand holding the gun and I saw it fire' |website=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/oct/20/muammar-gaddafi-killing-witnesses |access-date=24 September 2016 |quote=one fighter crouched in the dirt behind the frightened captive and sodomised him with a bayonet}}</ref>

==== 2011–2017: Syria ====
{{Main|Timber Sycamore|CIA activities in Syria|American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War}}

[[File:Syria in its region (claimed).svg|frameless|right]]

In April 2011, after the outbreak of the [[Syrian civil war]] in early 2011, three U.S. Senators, Republicans [[John McCain]] and [[Lindsey Graham]] and Independent [[Joe Lieberman]], urged President [[Barack Obama]] in a joint statement to "state unequivocally" that "it is time to go" for President [[Bashar al-Assad]].<ref>{{cite news|date=April 29, 2011|title=Assad must go, U.S. Republicans say|url=http://www.newspapers.com/image/426646115/|access-date=December 28, 2019|website=Newspapers.com|publisher=Agence France Presse|language=en|quote=We urge President Obama to state unequivocally, as he did in the case of (Libyan leader Moammar) Gadhafi and Egyptian president Hosni Mubarak — that it is time for Assad to go.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.commondreams.org/opinion/us-israel-syria|title=Opinion &#124; How the US and Israel Destroyed Syria and Called it Peace|last=Sachs|first=Jeffrey|date=December 12, 2024|work=Common Dreams|access-date=October 16, 2025}}</ref> In August 2011, the U.S. government called on Assad to "step aside" and imposed an [[oil embargo]] against the Syrian government.<ref>{{cite news |title=Calling for Regime Change in Syria |url=http://www.cfr.org/syria/calling-regime-change-syria/p25677 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209022621/https://www.cfr.org/syria/calling-regime-change-syria/p25677 |archive-date=December 9, 2020 |publisher=Council on Foreign Relations |access-date=March 22, 2025 |language=en |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Solomon |first1=Jay |last2=Malas |first2=Nour |last3=Norman |first3=Laurence |date=August 18, 2011 |title=World Leaders Call for Assad to Step Down |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424053111903639404576516144145940136 |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Tisdall |first=Simon |date=2015-01-25 |title=US changes its tune on Syrian regime change as Isis threat takes top priority |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/jan/25/us-syrian-regime-change-isis-priority |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Starting in 2013, the U.S. provided training, weapons, and money to vetted moderate Syrian rebels,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bowman |first=Tom |date=2014-04-23 |title=CIA Is Quietly Ramping Up Aid To Syrian Rebels, Sources Say |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/parallels/2014/04/23/306233248/cia-is-quietly-ramping-up-aid-to-syrian-rebels-sources-say |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Borger |first1=Julian |last2=Hopkins |first2=Nick |date=2013-03-08 |title=West training Syrian rebels in Jordan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2013/mar/08/west-training-syrian-rebels-jordan |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> and in 2014, the [[Supreme Military Council (Syria)|Supreme Military Council]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Abouzeid|first=Rania|date=September 26, 2013|title=Syrian Opposition Groups Stop Pretending|magazine=The New Yorker|url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/news-desk/syrian-opposition-groups-stop-pretending|url-status=live|access-date=May 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309033429/https://www.newyorker.com/news/news-desk/syrian-opposition-groups-stop-pretending|archive-date=March 9, 2018|issn=0028-792X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Atwan|first=Abdel Bari|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yHolDQAAQBAJ&q=digital+caliphate,+smc&pg=PA106|title=Islamic State: The Digital Caliphate|date=September 8, 2015|publisher=Univ of California Press|isbn=9780520289284|via=Google Books}}</ref> In 2015, Obama reaffirmed that "Assad must go".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Nelson|first=Colleen McCain|date=November 19, 2015|title=Obama Says Syrian Leader Bashar al-Assad Must Go|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/obama-says-syrian-leader-bashar-al-assad-must-go-1447925671|access-date=2019-12-28|website=The Wall Street Journal|language=en-US}}</ref>

In March 2017, Ambassador [[Nikki Haley]] told a group of reporters that the US's priority in Syria was no longer on "getting Assad out."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Nichols|first=Michelle|date=2017-03-31|title=U.S. priority on Syria no longer focused on 'getting Assad out': Haley|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-usa-haley-idUSKBN1712QL|access-date=2020-12-13}}</ref> Earlier that day at a news conference in [[Ankara]], Secretary of State [[Rex Tillerson]] also said that the "longer term status of President Assad will be decided by the Syrian people."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://au.news.yahoo.com/world/a/34856857/tillerson-says-assads-fate-up-to-syrian-people/#page1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330231421/https://au.news.yahoo.com/world/a/34856857/tillerson-says-assads-fate-up-to-syrian-people/#page1|archive-date=March 30, 2017|title=Tillerson says Assad's fate up to Syrian people|first1=Raziye|last1=Akkoc|first2=Fulya|last2=Ozerkan|date=March 30, 2017|publisher=Yahoo! 7 News}}</ref> While the [[US Defense Department]]'s program to aid predominantly [[Kurds|Kurdish]] rebels fighting the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] (ISIL) continued, it was revealed in July 2017 that US President [[Donald Trump]] had ordered a "phasing out" of the CIA's support for anti-Assad rebels.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jaffe|first1=Greg|last2=Entous|first2=Adam|date=July 19, 2017|title=Trump ends covert CIA program to arm anti-Assad rebels in Syria, a move sought by Moscow|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/trump-ends-covert-cia-program-to-arm-anti-assad-rebels-in-syria-a-move-sought-by-moscow/2017/07/19/b6821a62-6beb-11e7-96ab-5f38140b38cc_story.html|access-date=July 20, 2017|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> Ultimately, the Assad regime fell in the [[2024 Syrian opposition offensives]] spearheaded by [[Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham]] (HTS), the [[Syrian National Army]] (SNA), and the [[Southern Operations Room]] (SOR).

====2019: Bolivia====
{{Main|2019 Bolivian political crisis}}

In November 2019, Bolivian president [[Evo Morales]] resigned in what he and some US lawmakers called a coup; Morales then went into exile in Argentina.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/469906-trump-celebrates-resignation-of-bolivias-president/|title=Trump celebrates resignation of Bolivia's president|first=Brett|last=Samuels|date=November 11, 2019|work=The Hill}}</ref> Morales claimed the following month that the U.S. had plotted to oust him for choosing to seek lithium extraction partnerships with Russia and China.<ref>{{cite news|date=25 December 2019|title=Morales claims US orchestrated 'coup' to tap Bolivia's lithium|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/25/morales-claims-us-orchestrated-coup-to-tap-bolivias-lithium|work=Al Jazeera|access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref> In the aftermath, following the elections which brought back the socialist [[Movimiento al Socialismo]] to power, the coup narrative was proven false, but the U.S. still faced allegations that it had supported Morales' removal, including Justice Department pressure against MIT researchers whose work argued that Morales' reelection for a fourth term was legitimate.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://theintercept.com/2021/05/04/bolivia-coup-trump-mit-evo-morales/|title=DOJ Threatened MIT Researchers With Subpoena in Collaboration With Bolivian Coup Regime|first1=Ken|last1=Klippenstein|first2=Ryan|last2=Grim|date=May 4, 2021|website=The Intercept}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2025-12-17|title=Bolivia is still living through the aftermath of its 2019 coup|url=https://aldianews.com/en/politics/policy/bolivias-political-battles|date=11 December 2025|website=Al Día News}}</ref>

=== 2020s ===

==== 2025–2026: Greenland ====
{{Main|Greenland crisis}}
{{See also|Proposed United States acquisition of Greenland}}

As president in 2025, Trump renewed annexation threats against Greenland and refused to rule out military force. After the military intervention removing Maduro from office in 2026, Trump again threatened military action "whether they like it or not".<ref>{{cite web|last=Massad|first=Joseph|date=14 January 2026|title=From Venezuela to Iran, Trump's 'Donroe Doctrine' is a push to control the world's oil|work=Middle East Eye|url=https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/venezuela-iran-trumps-donroe-doctrine-escalates-us-push-control-worlds-oil|access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref> The United States in 2025 had also set up influencers and intelligence agencies to spy in Greenland and perform "covert influence operations", resulting in two US ambassador summons by Denmark.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Long|first1=Katherine|last2=Ward|first2=Alexander|date=6 May 2025|title=U.S. Orders Intelligence Agencies to Step Up Spying on Greenland|work=The Wall Street Journal|url=https://www.wsj.com/world/greenland-spying-us-intelligence-809c4ef2?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqed_-HJTn9XtR2vWcuGJZgXWUWBA10uzmSKTdrh3xJfiWeKj-3IeJndXxtIvSQ%3D&gaa_ts=69c6e041&gaa_sig=prNIFFyqZiXJ3vGtzWvEQ7mUeH0XPRAdR0uLQK71ZyVF9tSRT1cL6o5aYnnBENLgrC03JKyoGSa1gIojlIob-A%3D%3D|access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Gettleman|first1=Jeffrey|last2=Tekeli|first2=Maya|date=27 August 2025|title=Denmark Summons U.S. Envoy Over a Reported 'Influence Operation' in Greenland|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/27/world/europe/trump-denmark-greenland-us-embassy.html|access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref>

==== 2025–2026: Venezuela ====
{{Main|Operation Southern Spear|2026 United States intervention in Venezuela}}

{{See also|Proposed United States invasion of Venezuela}}
[[File:Venezuela in its region.svg|right|frameless]]

During the [[2025 United States naval deployment in the Caribbean]], Trump stated in October that he had authorized the CIA to conduct covert operations in Venezuela, which Maduro denounced.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-10-16 |title=Trump confirms the CIA is conducting covert operations inside Venezuela |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/10/16/g-s1-93677/trump-confirms-cia-operations-venezuela |access-date=2025-10-16 |work=NPR |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Debusmann Jr |first=Bernd |date=2025-10-16 |title=Trump says he authorised CIA in Venezuela as Maduro says 'no to regime change' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0ex1jq9pdvo |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 3 January 2026, the United States conducted airstrikes on multiple locations across Venezuela, including the capital city of [[Caracas]], and captured and exfiltrated Venezuelan President Maduro. President Donald Trump announced that Maduro had been captured alongside his wife [[Cilia Flores]] and flown out of the country.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kahn |first=Carrie |date=2026-01-03 |title=Trump claims U.S. strikes, Maduro captured as explosions hit Caracas |url=https://www.nprillinois.org/2026-01-03/trump-claims-u-s-strikes-maduro-captured-as-explosions-hit-caracas |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=NPR Illinois |language=en}}</ref> Attorney General [[Pam Bondi]] said both would face charges of [[narcoterrorism]] in the United States.<ref name="NMC">{{Cite web |last=Bergengruen |first=Vera |date=2026-01-03 |title=Maduro Faces Federal Drug-Trafficking Charges in U.S. |url=https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/venezuela-strikes/card/maduro-faces-federal-drug-trafficking-charges-in-u-s--hqFy8dcmWFBCuxLJNORl?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqcb_V-AORR4qcWHStQus4mU04kXSgXOLFqN6Y6z6IconlTchka87aY8u8NfYw%3D%3D&gaa_ts=695927fd&gaa_sig=eRBIc7yRJvyczvOCGHSI4ayIHX0nA8JqIAn30YLxVZWApSSDpzLteqBE0mM-6pnuOqASO0suL6Bs3p-mUahiaA%3D%3D |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en}}</ref> The government formerly led by Maduro remained in place, and Venezuela's [[Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)|Supreme Tribunal of Justice]] ordered Vice President [[Delcy Rodríguez]] to assume the presidency.<ref name="Reuters-01032026">{{cite news |date=3 January 2026 |title=Venezuela's top court orders VP Rodriguez to assume presidency |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelas-top-court-orders-vp-rodriguez-assume-presidency-2026-01-03/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=4 January 2026}}</ref> In just a few months, Rodríguez reshuffled roughly 40% of her cabinet, replacing 17 ministers and updating military leadership to install her own loyalists. Powerful Maduro loyalists, such as long-serving Defense Minister ⁠[[Vladimir Padrino López]] and Attorney General [[Tarek William Saab]], were stripped of their posts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-16 |title=Venezuela’s interim leader sacks Maduro ally Alex Saab as industry minister |url=https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20260116-venezuela-s-interim-leader-sacks-maduro-ally-alex-saab-as-industry-minister |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=France 24 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2026/03/18/venezuela/relevan-vladimir-padrino-ministro-defensa-orix|title=Delcy Rodríguez releva a Vladimir Padrino López como ministro de Defensa de Venezuela|language=es|work=[[CNN en Español]]|date=18 March 2026|access-date=18 March 2026}}</ref> This consolidation was further highlighted when Venezuela’s Minister of Industry and National Production, [[Alex Saab]], was also captured in February 2026 in a joint operation by American and Venezuelan intelligence agencies.<ref name="Second Arrest">{{Cite web |last=Freixes |first=Josep |date=2026-02-04 |title=FBI Arrests Alex Saab, Maduro's Alleged Front Man, in Venezuela |url=https://colombiaone.com/2026/02/04/fbi-arrests-alex-saab-maduro-venezuela/ |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=Colombia One: News from Colombia and the World |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Reuters Second Arrest">{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelan-official-saab-formerly-held-us-arrested-again-colombian-media-2026-02-04/|title=Maduro ally Saab, Venezuelan businessman once held in US, arrested again, US official says|access-date=February 4, 2026|work=Reuters}}</ref> In May 2026, he was deported to the US.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Venezuela deports Maduro ally Alex Saab to US |url=https://www.dw.com/en/venezuela-deports-maduro-ally-alex-saab-to-us/a-77184876 |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=dw.com |language=en}}</ref> Various analysts have called the US action "regime change."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2026/01/04/opinion/why-trump-bared-his-teeth-and-nabbed-venezuelas-maduro-and-its-not-just-drugs/|title=Why Trump bared his teeth and nabbed Venezuela's Maduro — and it's not just drugs|last=Schanzer|first=Jonathan|date=4 January 2025|work=New York Post}}</ref>

==== 2026: Cuba ====
{{Main|2026 Cuban crisis}}

During its intervention in Venezuela, the US caused an oil shortage in Cuba with the aim to remove the current government by the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=de Córdoba |first=José |date=22 January 2026 |title=The U.S. Is Actively Seeking Regime Change in Cuba by the End of the Year|url=https://www.wsj.com/world/americas/the-u-s-is-actively-seeking-regime-change-in-cuba-by-the-end-of-the-year-1d0f178a |archive-date=31 January 2026 |access-date= |website=The Wall Street Journal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260131125848/https://www.wsj.com/world/americas/the-u-s-is-actively-seeking-regime-change-in-cuba-by-the-end-of-the-year-1d0f178a |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 2026: Iran ====
{{Main|2026 Iran war}}
{{see also|Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war}}

In February 2026, the United States, alongside [[Israel]], launched a [[2026 Israeli–United States strikes on Iran|major attack on Iran]] with the stated goal of regime change.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Sanger|first=David E.|author-link=David E. Sanger|date=February 28, 2026|title=For Trump, the Iran Attack Is the Ultimate War of Choice|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/28/us/politics/trump-iran-attack.html|url-access=subscription|access-date=March 1, 2026}}</ref> On 28 February 2026, Iranian supreme leader [[Ali Khamenei]] was [[Assassination of Ali Khamenei|killed]] in an Israeli missile strike.<ref>{{Cite news|title= Iran confirms Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei dead after US-Israeli attacks|url= https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/28/irans-supreme-leader-ali-khamenei-killed-in-us-israeli-attacks-reports|work=Al Jazeera|date=February 28, 2026|access-date=March 6, 2026}}</ref>
